title: Wyatt Earp | The Man Behind the Legend (English Listening Practice)
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 大家好，大家好，大家好，欢迎收听 Leonardo English 出品的 English Learning for Curious Minds。在这档节目里，你可以一边听引人入胜的故事、了解这个世界稀奇古怪又精彩纷呈的事情，一边提升你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I’m Alastair Budge, and today we are going to start a three-part mini-series called Tales from the Wild West.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们要开始一个三集的迷你系列节目，叫做《荒野西部的故事》(Tales from the Wild West)。

sentences.en: Instead of talking about the history of the Wild West, we’re going to learn about it through the stories of three famous historical characters.
sentences.zh: 这次我们不打算平铺直叙地讲荒野西部的历史，而是通过三位著名历史人物的故事来了解这段历史。

sentences.en: In this episode, part one, it’ll be Wyatt Earp: a man who, to quote his Wikipedia page, was at various points a Lawman, a buffalo hunter, a saloon keeper, a miner, a brothel keeper, and a boxing referee, which is a kind of resume you just don’t see nowadays.
sentences.zh: 在这一集，也就是第一部分，主角是 Wyatt Earp：用他维基百科页面上的话说，他先后当过执法官、猎捕野牛的猎人、酒馆老板、矿工、妓院老板，还做过拳击裁判——这样的履历放在今天可是见不到了。

sentences.en: Next up it’ll be Bass Reeves: a man born into slavery who went on to become one of the most feared and successful lawmen in American history.
sentences.zh: 接下来是 Bass Reeves：一个生来为奴的人，后来却成为美国历史上最令人畏惧、也最成功的执法官之一。

sentences.en: And in part three, it’ll be Geronimo: the Native American leader whose life and surrender tell a very different story about the reality of life in the Wild West.
sentences.zh: 第三部分的主角是 Geronimo：这位美洲原住民领袖的一生和他的投降，讲述了一个关于荒野西部真实生活截然不同的故事。

sentences.en: OK then, let’s not waste a minute, and get right into it.
sentences.zh: 好了，废话不多说，我们马上开始。

sentences.en: It is the 26th of October, 1881. The time is around half past two in the afternoon.
sentences.zh: 时间是1881年10月26日，下午两点半左右。

sentences.en: In a narrow vacant lot beside a photography studio in Tombstone, Arizona, eight men are standing close together.
sentences.zh: 在亚利桑那州汤姆斯通(Tombstone)一家照相馆旁边的一块狭窄空地上，八名男子紧紧站在一起。

sentences.en: Close enough to touch. Some are pointing their guns.
sentences.zh: 彼此近得几乎能碰到对方。有人已经举起了枪。

sentences.en: Others have not yet drawn their weapons.
sentences.zh: 另一些人还没有拔出武器。

sentences.en: Thirty seconds later, it is over. One man has disappeared into a nearby photography studio.
sentences.zh: 三十秒后，一切结束了。一名男子已经躲进了附近的照相馆。

sentences.en: Three men are dead on the ground. Three others are wounded.
sentences.zh: 三人倒在地上死去，另外三人受了伤。

sentences.en: One man, Wyatt Earp, is standing without a scratch.
sentences.zh: 只有一个人——Wyatt Earp——毫发无损地站在那里。

sentences.en: This is the story of the gunfight at the OK Corral, which has gone down as perhaps the most iconic scene in the history of the Wild West.
sentences.zh: 这就是“OK 牧场枪战”(the gunfight at the OK Corral)的故事，它可以说是荒野西部历史上最具标志性的一幕。

sentences.en: If you have seen one of the film adaptations of it, like Tombstone or the Wyatt Earp film, the scene will be familiar.
sentences.zh: 如果你看过根据这段历史改编的电影，比如《汤姆斯通》(Tombstone)或者《怀特·厄普》(Wyatt Earp)，这个场景你一定不会陌生。

sentences.en: But even if you haven’t, you can probably picture something like it.
sentences.zh: 但即便你没看过，大概也能想象出类似的画面。

sentences.en: A long dusty street. Two groups of men walking slowly toward each other in the afternoon heat.
sentences.zh: 一条尘土飞扬的长街。两群人在午后的酷热中缓缓迎面走来。

sentences.en: Flies buzzing around. The clink of spurs.
sentences.zh: 苍蝇嗡嗡飞舞，马刺叮当作响。

sentences.en: A sheriff’s badge glinting in the sun. This is the Hollywood version.
sentences.zh: 警长徽章在阳光下闪闪发光。这就是好莱坞版本的故事。

sentences.en: The real version was somewhat different, as we’ll come to discover.
sentences.zh: 而真实的版本却有所不同，这一点我们接下来就会发现。

sentences.en: Now, before we get to the story of Wyatt Earp, we need some background.
sentences.zh: 不过，在讲 Wyatt Earp 的故事之前，我们需要先了解一些背景。

sentences.en: Let’s start with the phrase. The phrase “Wild West” probably conjures up a very specific image.
sentences.zh: 先从这个说法本身说起。“荒野西部”(Wild West)这个词，大概会让人联想到一幅非常具体的画面。

sentences.en: Cattle. Saloons. Outlaws and sheriffs. Everyone looking like they wouldn’t say no to a hot bath.
sentences.zh: 牛群、酒馆、亡命之徒和警长，每个人看上去都像是很久没洗过热水澡了。

sentences.en: The Wild West, as historians generally use the term, refers to a specific period in American history: roughly from the end of the Civil War in 1865 to the early 1890s, although some people have it starting earlier and finishing later.
sentences.zh: 历史学家通常所说的“荒野西部”，指的是美国历史上一个特定的时期：大致从1865年南北战争结束到19世纪90年代初，不过也有人认为它开始得更早、结束得更晚。

sentences.en: This was the period when the United States was expanding westward at a ferocious pace, pushing into territories that had been home to Native American peoples for centuries, and absorbing land that had until recently belonged to Mexico.
sentences.zh: 在这段时期，美国以极快的速度向西扩张，深入几个世纪以来一直是美洲原住民家园的土地，并吞并了不久前还属于墨西哥的领土。

sentences.en: What made it “wild”, from the perspective of the Americans arriving there, was the absence of established institutions.
sentences.zh: 在到达那里的美国人看来，之所以称其为“荒野”，是因为那里缺乏成熟的制度。

sentences.en: There were no courts. No reliable police forces.
sentences.zh: 没有法庭，没有可靠的警力。

sentences.en: No prisons. No property registries. Nothing.
sentences.zh: 没有监狱，没有产权登记，什么都没有。

sentences.en: It was, essentially, a free-for-all. Towns appeared almost overnight, and were typically built near to places where silver had been discovered [called silver strikes], or along cattle routes, or where new railway track had been laid.
sentences.zh: 本质上，那里就是一片弱肉强食的天地。城镇几乎一夜之间冒出来，通常建在发现银矿的地方(所谓的“银矿发现地”)，或者沿着牛群运输路线，又或者铁路新铺设到的地方。

sentences.en: And the men who came to these places tended to be labourers, gamblers, former soldiers, and what we might call “drifters”: men who moved from place to place without settling anywhere.
sentences.zh: 来到这些地方的人，大多是劳工、赌徒、退伍军人，还有我们可以称之为“流浪汉”的人：他们四处漂泊，从不在一个地方定居。

sentences.en: Wyatt Earp was one of them. He was born in 1848, in Monmouth, Illinois, a small town in the American Midwest.
sentences.zh: Wyatt Earp 就是其中一员。他于1848年出生在美国中西部伊利诺伊州的小镇蒙茅斯(Monmouth)。

sentences.en: He was the fourth of five brothers, and the family moved often during his childhood: Illinois to Iowa to Missouri to California and back again.
sentences.zh: 他是五兄弟中的老四，童年时期全家经常搬迁：从伊利诺伊到爱荷华，再到密苏里、加利福尼亚，然后又搬了回去。

sentences.en: History remembers him as a legendary lawman, a man who stood up for good in the face of lawlessness, but the reality is a little more complicated.
sentences.zh: 历史上把他记作一位传奇执法官，一个在无法无天的环境中挺身而出、匡扶正义的人，但现实要复杂得多。

sentences.en: In his twenties, he worked as a buffalo hunter on the Kansas plains, when the vast herds that had roamed the great plains for centuries were being systematically slaughtered for their hides.
sentences.zh: 二十多岁时，他在堪萨斯平原上当过猎捕野牛的猎人，当时那些在大平原上漫游了几个世纪的庞大兽群，正被有计划地大批猎杀以获取兽皮。

sentences.en: Then, he drove stagecoaches: horse-drawn vehicles that carried passengers and mail across long distances before the railways reached everywhere.
sentences.zh: 后来，他又当过驿马车车夫：在铁路还没有铺到各地之前，这种马车负责长途运送乘客和邮件。

sentences.en: He was a taxi driver, essentially. In 1871, he was arrested on a charge of horse theft, which was a serious crime at the time, and for which execution wasn’t an uncommon sentence.
sentences.zh: 说白了就是个“出租车司机”。1871年，他因盗马罪被捕，这在当时是重罪，判处死刑也不是什么稀罕事。

sentences.en: Luckily for him, and for our story, he managed to escape from jail, and skipped town.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是——对他本人，也对我们这个故事来说——他成功越狱并逃离了小镇。

sentences.en: And again, fortunately for our story, the 1870s was not a time of extensive background checks and synchronised criminal databases, so Earp was able to get various jobs as a lawman, a sort of police officer.
sentences.zh: 同样幸运的是,19世纪70年代还没有严格的背景调查和联网的犯罪数据库，所以 Earp 后来还能陆续谋得几份执法官(相当于警察)的工作。

sentences.en: First in Wichita and then in Dodge City, both in Kansas, where he served as a deputy marshal.
sentences.zh: 先是在堪萨斯州的威奇托(Wichita)，后来又在道奇城(Dodge City)，他在那里担任副警长(deputy marshal)。

sentences.en: So, he has had what we might call a “portfolio career” so far: buffalo hunter, stagecoach driver, horse thief, and now deputy marshal.
sentences.zh: 所以到目前为止，他的履历可以说相当“多元”：猎野牛的猎人、驿马车车夫、盗马贼，如今又成了副警长。

sentences.en: He was also, it would appear, involved in prostitution, and was arrested several times for running a brothel.
sentences.zh: 看起来，他似乎也涉足过色情行业，曾多次因经营妓院被捕。

sentences.en: And, to complete the picture, he was a frequent gambler, spending much of his time in saloons and playing a card game called faro.
sentences.zh: 而为了让这幅画像更完整：他还是个常年赌博的人，大部分时间都泡在酒馆里，玩一种叫法罗(faro)的纸牌游戏。

sentences.en: He was actually quite good, he would later claim, and made more money through gambling than he did through his official job as a lawman.
sentences.zh: 他后来声称自己牌技相当不错，靠赌博赚的钱比当执法官的正职收入还要多。

sentences.en: By 1879, he had made his way to a town called Tombstone, in Arizona, along with three of his five brothers.
sentences.zh: 到1879年，他和五个兄弟中的三个一起，来到了亚利桑那州一座名叫汤姆斯通(Tombstone)的小镇。

sentences.en: One brother, Virgil, was already there, and had taken up the position of town marshal, the local law enforcement chief.
sentences.zh: 他的哥哥 Virgil 已经先到了那里，并当上了镇治安官(town marshal)，也就是当地的执法负责人。

sentences.en: Virgil had not just arrived first; he had effectively sent for his brothers.
sentences.zh: Virgil 不仅先到一步，实际上还是他把弟弟们叫过去的。

sentences.en: As town marshal, he could appoint deputies, and he hired family.
sentences.zh: 作为镇治安官，他有权任命副手，于是他雇用了自己的家人。

sentences.en: It was nepotism, essentially, but it was also practical: in a town with no reliable law enforcement, men who would take a bullet for you were worth more than qualified strangers.
sentences.zh: 说白了这就是任人唯亲，但也确实很实际：在一个缺乏可靠执法力量的小镇里，愿意为你挡子弹的人，比一个有资历的陌生人更值得信赖。

sentences.en: James, the oldest of the four, who was quieter and more reserved than the others, he worked in a saloon.
sentences.zh: 四兄弟中年纪最大的 James 性格比其他人更安静、更内敛，他在一家酒馆工作。

sentences.en: Another, Morgan, arrived around the same time as Wyatt.
sentences.zh: 另一个兄弟 Morgan，差不多和 Wyatt 同时抵达。

sentences.en: And Warren, the youngest, came later. Tombstone had struck silver in 1877, and by 1881 it was one of the most prosperous cities in the area, with a population of several thousand people.
sentences.zh: 最小的弟弟 Warren 则是后来才到的。汤姆斯通在1877年发现了银矿，到1881年，它已经成为这一带最繁荣的城市之一，人口有好几千人。

sentences.en: It had newspapers. An opera house. A telegraph office.
sentences.zh: 镇上有报纸，有歌剧院，还有电报局。

sentences.en: It was pretty big by frontier standards.
sentences.zh: 以边疆小镇的标准来说，这已经算是相当大的城市了。

sentences.en: It also had a serious problem. The problem was the Cowboys.
sentences.zh: 但它也有一个严重的问题，这个问题就是“牛仔帮”(the Cowboys)。

sentences.en: The Cowboys, which is what they were actually called, they were a loose network of cattle thieves and smugglers who operated out of the surrounding hills and valleys.
sentences.zh: “牛仔帮”确实就是他们的名字，这是一个松散的团伙网络，由盗牛贼和走私犯组成，活动范围遍布周围的山丘和山谷。

sentences.en: They stole livestock in Mexico and sold it on the American side of the border.
sentences.zh: 他们在墨西哥偷牲畜，然后拿到美国一侧的边境贩卖。

sentences.en: They robbed stagecoaches. They intimidated people.
sentences.zh: 他们打劫驿马车，恐吓当地居民。

sentences.en: They were not organised in any formal sense, but they had numbers, and local political support.
sentences.zh: 他们算不上正式的组织，但人数众多，而且在当地政界也有支持者。

sentences.en: And as you might imagine, they hated the Earp brothers, and had a running feud that had been building for months.
sentences.zh: 可以想见，他们对 Earp 兄弟恨之入骨，双方的积怨已经持续了好几个月。

sentences.en: The tension was about money and power and political allegiance.
sentences.zh: 这种紧张关系的根源在于金钱、权力和政治立场。

sentences.en: The county sheriff, a man named Johnny Behan, was sympathetic to the Cowboys.
sentences.zh: 县警长 Johnny Behan 对“牛仔帮”抱有同情。

sentences.en: He had grown up among ranching people and shared their wariness of the Earp brothers, who he saw as outsiders with their own agenda, which they were, really.
sentences.zh: 他从小在牧场人家中长大，和他们一样对 Earp 兄弟心存戒备，认为这几兄弟是心怀私利的外来者——事实也确实如此。

sentences.en: Virgil Earp, as Tombstone’s town marshal, was not sympathetic to the Cowboys at all.
sentences.zh: 身为汤姆斯通镇治安官的 Virgil Earp，对“牛仔帮”完全没有半分好感。

sentences.en: And Wyatt Earp had ambitions to become county sheriff himself.
sentences.zh: 而 Wyatt Earp 自己则一心想当上县警长。

sentences.en: In other words, he had his sights on Behan’s job.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他盯上的正是 Behan 的位子。

sentences.en: There was also a personal dimension. Johnny Behan and Wyatt Earp had been involved with the same woman, Josephine Marcus, a theatre performer who had been briefly engaged to Behan before she broke it off.
sentences.zh: 这其中还有私人恩怨。Johnny Behan 和 Wyatt Earp 曾同时与一位名叫 Josephine Marcus 的女演员有过感情纠葛，她曾短暂与 Behan 订婚，但后来解除了婚约。

sentences.en: By the autumn of 1881, the feud between the Earps and the Cowboys had been simmering for long enough.
sentences.zh: 到1881年秋天，Earp 家族与“牛仔帮”之间的宿怨已经积压了很久。

sentences.en: On the morning of October 26th, Virgil Earp received word that several Cowboys were in town and visibly armed, which technically violated Tombstone’s ordinance, its local law, against carrying firearms within the city limits.
sentences.zh: 10月26日清晨，Virgil Earp 得到消息，说有几名“牛仔帮”成员进了城，而且公然携带武器，这严格来说违反了汤姆斯通镇关于禁止在城区携带枪支的地方法规。

sentences.en: Virgil assembled a small group: Wyatt, Morgan, and their friend Doc Holliday, a gambler and gunfighter who was one of the most feared men on the frontier.
sentences.zh: Virgil 召集了一支小队：Wyatt、Morgan，还有他们的朋友 Doc Holliday——一位赌徒兼枪手，也是边疆地区最令人畏惧的人物之一。

sentences.en: The four of them walked toward the vacant lot where they had heard the Cowboys were.
sentences.zh: 四人朝着据说“牛仔帮”所在的那块空地走去。

sentences.en: What happened next is disputed in almost every account.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事情，几乎在每一份记述中都存在争议。

sentences.en: Who fired first? Was there a verbal warning?
sentences.zh: 是谁先开的枪？有没有口头警告？

sentences.en: Were the Cowboys trying to surrender? Were the Cowboys even armed?
sentences.zh: “牛仔帮”当时是不是想投降？他们到底有没有带武器？

sentences.en: Virgil Earp later said he told them to give up their weapons.
sentences.zh: Virgil Earp 后来说，他曾命令对方交出武器。

sentences.en: The Cowboys’ side said no such offer was made.
sentences.zh: “牛仔帮”这边则表示根本没有这回事。

sentences.en: What everyone agrees on is this: it lasted roughly thirty seconds.
sentences.zh: 唯一没有争议的一点是：整场枪战大约只持续了三十秒。

sentences.en: On the Cowboys side, three were killed outright.
sentences.zh: “牛仔帮”一方，三人当场毙命。

sentences.en: On the other side, Virgil and Morgan Earp were both wounded.
sentences.zh: 另一方，Virgil 和 Morgan Earp 都受了伤。

sentences.en: Doc Holliday was grazed. Wyatt walked away without injury.
sentences.zh: Doc Holliday 只是被擦伤，Wyatt 则毫发无损地走了出来。

sentences.en: There were no celebrations among the town’s residents.
sentences.zh: 小镇居民之间没有任何欢庆的气氛。

sentences.en: The Earps and Holliday were charged with murder.
sentences.zh: Earp 兄弟和 Holliday 被以谋杀罪起诉。

sentences.en: There was a trial, which ultimately ruled in their favour, finding that Virgil had been acting in his capacity as town marshal and that the shootings were justified.
sentences.zh: 案件经过审理，最终判决对他们有利，认定 Virgil 当时是在履行镇治安官的职责，枪击行为属于正当行为。

sentences.en: But the community was divided. Half of Tombstone saw the Earps as law enforcers.
sentences.zh: 但小镇上的民众意见分裂。有一半人把 Earp 兄弟视为执法者。

sentences.en: The other half saw them as men who had used their badges to settle a private score.
sentences.zh: 另一半人则认为，他们不过是借着警徽的名义，私下寻仇了结恩怨。

sentences.en: There were elements of truth to both arguments.
sentences.zh: 两种说法都各有几分道理。

sentences.en: Virgil Earp was the town marshal, and the Cowboys were breaking the rules about carrying weapons inside the town.
sentences.zh: Virgil Earp 确实是镇治安官，“牛仔帮”确实违反了城内携带武器的规定。

sentences.en: But the Earps had spent months feuding with the Cowboys.
sentences.zh: 但 Earp 兄弟也确实和“牛仔帮”结怨已久，持续了好几个月。

sentences.en: And the badge gave them the authority to do something about it.
sentences.zh: 而警徽，则给了他们采取行动的权力。

sentences.en: And this shootout was just the start of a bitter tit-for-tat vendetta.
sentences.zh: 而这场枪战，只是一场以牙还牙、恩怨不休的复仇的开端。

sentences.en: Two months later, in December 1881, Virgil Earp was ambushed outside a saloon late at night.
sentences.zh: 两个月后,1881年12月，Virgil Earp 深夜在一家酒馆外遭到伏击。

sentences.en: Shotgun blasts hit his left arm. He survived, but his arm was permanently disabled.
sentences.zh: 霰弹枪击中了他的左臂，他保住了性命，但左臂从此终身残废。

sentences.en: Three months after that, in March 1882, Morgan Earp was shot through a window while playing billiards in a saloon.
sentences.zh: 又过了三个月,1882年3月，Morgan Earp 在一家酒馆打台球时，被人隔着窗户开枪射中。

sentences.en: Two bullets hit him. He died within the hour, on the floor, in his brother Wyatt’s arms.
sentences.zh: 两颗子弹击中了他，不到一小时后，他就倒在地板上，死在哥哥 Wyatt 的怀里。

sentences.en: And what followed was not due legal process, it was revenge, pure and simple.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事，不是什么正当的法律程序，而是彻头彻尾的复仇。

sentences.en: Wyatt Earp, with a small group of men that included Doc Holliday, Warren Earp, and several others, rode out in pursuit of the men they held responsible.
sentences.zh: Wyatt Earp 带着一小队人马，包括 Doc Holliday、Warren Earp 以及其他几人，骑马出发追杀他们认定的凶手。

sentences.en: Over the following three weeks, they hunted and killed at least four of them; at a railway station, in the hills, and at a water source.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的三个星期里，他们追猎并杀死了至少四人，地点分别是在一座火车站、山丘之间，以及一处水源旁。

sentences.en: These were not arrests. There was no due process.
sentences.zh: 这些都不是逮捕行动，也没有任何正当程序可言。

sentences.en: No trial. This was the “Wild” West, but even here, this crossed a line.
sentences.zh: 没有审判。这里是“狂野”的西部，但即便如此，这也已经越过了底线。

sentences.en: A warrant was issued for Wyatt Earp’s arrest on charges of murder.
sentences.zh: 当局发出了逮捕令，以谋杀罪通缉 Wyatt Earp。

sentences.en: He fled Arizona Territory, rode north into Colorado and never returned to Arizona.
sentences.zh: 他逃离了亚利桑那领地，一路北上进入科罗拉多，从此再也没有回过亚利桑那。

sentences.en: He bounced from place to place, chasing the next opportunity.
sentences.zh: 此后他辗转各地，四处寻找下一个机会。

sentences.en: Colorado, then Texas. San Diego in the late 1880s, where he ran saloons and became a property speculator.
sentences.zh: 先是科罗拉多，然后是德克萨斯。19世纪80年代末又到了圣迭戈，他在那里经营酒馆，还做起了地产投机生意。

sentences.en: He made good money, then lost most of it when the land boom collapsed.
sentences.zh: 他赚了不少钱，但随着地产热潮崩盘，又把大部分都亏了回去。

sentences.en: In 1896, he made the news after refereeing a heavyweight boxing championship fight in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 1896年，他因为在旧金山担任一场重量级拳击冠军赛的裁判而登上了新闻。

sentences.en: The bout ended controversially, with Earp awarding the match to the fighter who appeared to be losing, and the national newspapers accused him of fixing the result.
sentences.zh: 那场比赛的结果充满争议，Earp 把胜利判给了看起来明显落于下风的一方，全国各地的报纸都指责他操纵了比赛结果。

sentences.en: Then came Alaska during the gold rush of 1897, where he ran a saloon and reportedly made the equivalent of several million dollars in today’s money.
sentences.zh: 接着是1897年淘金热期间的阿拉斯加，他在那里开了一家酒馆，据说赚到了相当于今天几百万美元的财富。

sentences.en: Then it was Nevada, still gambling. And finally Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 然后是内华达，他依旧在赌桌上打转。最后，他来到了洛杉矶。

sentences.en: And it would be in Los Angeles that he would find himself remade, turned into something that he never was.
sentences.zh: 而正是在洛杉矶，他将被彻底重塑，变成一个他从来都不曾真正是的人。

sentences.en: Los Angeles, of course, is the home of Hollywood, which was, by the 1910s and 1920s, the centre of the American film industry.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，洛杉矶正是好莱坞的所在地，而到了20世纪10年代和20年代，好莱坞已经是美国电影产业的中心。

sentences.en: The dominant genre was the Western. Cowboys and sheriffs and open plains.
sentences.zh: 当时最主流的电影类型是西部片：牛仔、警长，还有辽阔的平原。

sentences.en: Clear moral lines. The good man with the gun.
sentences.zh: 善恶分明，手持枪械的正义之人。

sentences.en: Now, Earp had been thinking about fame and how it worked for a long time.
sentences.zh: 其实，Earp 早就一直在琢磨名气这回事，以及它究竟是怎么运作的。

sentences.en: A generation earlier, he’d seen how Wild West figures had become household names through dime novels, the cheap, sensational books sold for about ten cents.
sentences.zh: 早在一代人之前，他就见识过荒野西部的人物是如何通过“十分钱小说”(dime novels)——那种廉价、情节夸张、只卖十美分的书——变得家喻户晓的。

sentences.en: A man who got written up in the right way could become famous across the country, have his name outlast him.
sentences.zh: 一个人只要被以恰当的方式写进书里，就能在全国范围内声名大噪，甚至让自己的名字比自己活得更久。

sentences.en: Earp had watched it happen to others and wanted it to happen to him.
sentences.zh: Earp 眼看着这种事发生在别人身上，也渴望有朝一日能发生在自己身上。

sentences.en: And now Hollywood was doing the same thing, albeit on a far larger scale.
sentences.zh: 如今，好莱坞正在做着同样的事情，只是规模要大得多。

sentences.en: And importantly, Earp had something that almost nobody else on those film sets had: real-life experience.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，Earp 拥有一样几乎在那些片场里没有人拥有的东西：真实的亲身经历。

sentences.en: He was actually there. They were making movies about a period he had lived through.
sentences.zh: 他是真正在场的人，他们拍的正是他亲身经历过的那个年代。

sentences.en: He became a regular visitor to Western sets, and got to know some of the biggest stars of the era, not just because he enjoyed it, but because he understood what Hollywood could do.
sentences.zh: 他成了西部片片场的常客，还结识了那个年代一些最大牌的明星，这不仅仅是因为他乐在其中，更是因为他明白好莱坞能为他做什么。

sentences.en: These were the people who would decide whose story got told.
sentences.zh: 这些人，正是决定谁的故事会被讲述出来的人。

sentences.en: He advised them on how to carry themselves, how to hold a pistol, how a real lawman moved.
sentences.zh: 他给演员们指点该如何举止、如何握枪、真正的执法官走路和行动是什么样子。

sentences.en: And all the while, he was making a case for himself as a quintessential hero of the Wild West.
sentences.zh: 而与此同时，他也在不断为自己树立形象，把自己塑造成荒野西部典型的英雄人物。

sentences.en: But he had a problem. The record as it existed was not the one he wanted told.
sentences.zh: 但他有一个难题：已经存在的历史记录，并不是他想让世人知道的那个版本。

sentences.en: In the newspapers of the Southwest, he had been reported as a murderer: a man who had used his badge to pursue a private vendetta and then fled justice.
sentences.zh: 在美国西南部的报纸上，他曾被报道成一个杀人凶手：一个借警徽之名追求私人复仇、事后又逃避法律制裁的人。

sentences.en: The boxing scandal had brought his name to a national audience, but for the wrong reasons.
sentences.zh: 那场拳击丑闻虽然让他的名字传遍全国，但原因却并不光彩。

sentences.en: In other words, the name Wyatt Earp was associated with crime, match-fixing, and general skulduggery, dodgy dealing; he wanted to be remembered as a hero.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，“Wyatt Earp”这个名字被人和犯罪、操纵比赛、以及各种见不得光的勾当联系在一起；而他想要的，是被人们当作英雄铭记。

sentences.en: So, he got to work trying to change the historical record.
sentences.zh: 于是，他开始着手改写历史记录。

sentences.en: He tried first with a writer named John Flood, who spent years working on a manuscript about Earp’s life.
sentences.zh: 他最初找了一位名叫 John Flood 的作家合作，后者花了数年时间撰写一部关于 Earp 生平的手稿。

sentences.en: Flood was reportedly a terrible writer, and the book was rejected by every publisher it was sent to.
sentences.zh: 据说 Flood 的文笔实在糟糕，这本书投给的每一家出版社都拒绝了它。

sentences.en: Then, in the last years of his life, Earp found a journalist named Stuart Lake.
sentences.zh: 后来，在人生的最后几年，Earp 找到了一位名叫 Stuart Lake 的记者。

sentences.en: Lake was ambitious, a gifted writer, and willing to sit with the old man and take down everything he said.
sentences.zh: Lake 野心勃勃，文笔出色，也愿意坐下来陪着这位老人，把他说的每一句话都记录下来。

sentences.en: Earp talked. Lake listened and took notes.
sentences.zh: Earp 讲述，Lake 倾听并做笔记。

sentences.en: Between them, they worked for the definitive account: the one that would fix his reputation for good.
sentences.zh: 两人齐心协力，想要打造出一部“权威版本”——一部能彻底扭转他名声的传记。

sentences.en: Earp died on the 13th of January, 1929, before the book was finished.
sentences.zh: Earp 在1929年1月13日去世，那时这本书还没有完成。

sentences.en: He was eighty years old. By this time, the gunfight at the OK Corral was almost fifty years in the past and barely remembered.
sentences.zh: 他享年八十岁。此时，OK 牧场枪战已经过去了将近五十年，几乎无人记得。

sentences.en: But two years later, he and the gunfight would be brought back to life.
sentences.zh: 但两年后，他和那场枪战都将被重新唤醒，再度“活”了过来。

sentences.en: Lake published his book: Wyatt Earp: Frontier Marshal.
sentences.zh: Lake 出版了他的书：《怀特·厄普：边疆治安官》(Wyatt Earp: Frontier Marshal)。

sentences.en: The Earp of this book, a book that was presented as an accurate biography, was not the gambling, drifting, horse-thieving, pimping, revenge-killing, complicated man of the historical record.
sentences.zh: 这本书号称是一部真实准确的传记，但书中的 Earp 已经不再是历史记录中那个嗜赌、漂泊、偷马、拉皮条、复仇杀人的复杂人物。

sentences.en: He was a hero. A symbol. The embodiment of law and order in a lawless land.
sentences.zh: 他成了一位英雄，一个符号，一个在无法无天之地体现法律与秩序的化身。

sentences.en: The book was a bestseller. It was adapted for film almost immediately, and the adaptations kept coming.
sentences.zh: 这本书大获畅销，几乎立刻就被搬上了银幕，此后改编作品接连不断。

sentences.en: John Ford’s My Darling Clementine in 1946.
sentences.zh: 1946年，约翰·福特(John Ford)执导的《侠骨柔情》(My Darling Clementine)。

sentences.en: Gunfight at the O.K. Corral in 1957. And then, in 1993 and 1994, two major Hollywood films, Tombstone and Wyatt Earp, brought the story to yet another generation.
sentences.zh: 1957年的《龙争虎斗 OK 镇》(Gunfight at the O.K. Corral)。而后在1993年和1994年，两部重量级好莱坞电影《汤姆斯通》(Tombstone)和《怀特·厄普》(Wyatt Earp)又把这个故事带给了新一代观众。

sentences.en: With each retelling, the thirty-second argument over a town firearms ordinance became a defining battle between civilisation and lawlessness.
sentences.zh: 每重述一次，这场因城镇枪支条例引发、只持续了三十秒的争执，就被塑造得更像是一场文明与无法无天之间的决定性对决。

sentences.en: A drifting gambler with a chequered past became the man who tamed the West.
sentences.zh: 一个有着不光彩过去、四处漂泊的赌徒，就此变成了驯服西部的那个人。

sentences.en: So, to wrap things up, Wyatt Earp died in 1929 without ever clearing his name, without ever seeing his book published, without ever appearing on a cinema screen.
sentences.zh: 所以，总结一下：Wyatt Earp 于1929年去世时，始终没能洗清自己的名声，没能看到自己的书出版，也没能在电影银幕上露面。

sentences.en: Within a few years of his death, he was one of the most famous figures of the American West.
sentences.zh: 而在他去世后短短几年内，他就成了美国西部历史上最有名的人物之一。

sentences.en: The Wild West had found its hero. The only problem was that he’d never really existed.
sentences.zh: 荒野西部找到了自己的英雄，唯一的问题是，这个英雄其实从未真正存在过。

sentences.en: OK, then, that is it for today’s episode: the first part of our three-part mini-series on Tales from the Wild West.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天的节目就到这里，这是我们三集迷你系列《荒野西部的故事》的第一部分。

sentences.en: Next up, we’ll meet Bass Reeves: born into slavery, three thousand arrests to his name, but was almost forgotten to history.
sentences.zh: 下一集，我们将认识 Bass Reeves：生来为奴，一生逮捕过三千人，却几乎被历史遗忘。

sentences.en: And in part three, we’ll look at the Wild West from an entirely different angle: through the story of the Apache leader Geronimo.
sentences.zh: 而在第三部分，我们将从一个完全不同的角度审视荒野西部：通过阿帕奇领袖 Geronimo 的故事。

sentences.en: You’ve been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期 Leonardo English 出品的 English Learning for Curious Minds。

sentences.en: I’m Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I’ll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，祝你平安，我们下期节目再见。
